historical_claims.anchor: The founding moral of Spider-Man is often summarized as the connection between great power and great responsibility.
The classic arrangement with J. Jonah Jameson's newspaper is funny because a man who performs public service ends up selling evidence of himself to a hostile employer.
The high-school bully Flash Thompson can admire Spider-Man and insult Peter.
Doctor Octopus is an intellect whose mechanical extensions allow extraordinary physical action;
Consider the Master Planner climax in The Amazing Spider-Man number thirty-three.
Gwen's death had force partly because the continuity allowed it to matter.
Venom, introduced later from the history of Peter's alien costume, turns intimacy, imitation, and resentment into a bodily threat.

description: Examines literary and visual analysis using the early comics as the principal reference.
